data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace, a Series G-stage space and aerospace company founded by Bryan Dean, is evaluated against a comparative set of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE. The target has raised $20M to date.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $20M as a valuation proxy ($41M implied enterprise value), a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G-to-later-stage advancement yields $51M. This method is grounded in historical capital infusion patterns at this stage rather than market multiples. Peer-median analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within the aerospace sector—only one adjacent-stage peer was identified, falling below the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring using the Space & Aerospace P/S median of 27.4x across six public tickers cannot be deployed absent the target's revenue figures, which private companies typically withhold.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $44M (low) to $59M (high), with a median point of $51M. This range rests on a single applicable method and thus carries material uncertainty around the appropriate stage multiplier and the $41M implied base value. Revenue disclosure or identification of additional same-stage private comparables would strengthen conviction in this estimate.
